carpien.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
carpien.whatYouFeel: Pins and needles and numbness in the thumb, index and middle fingers, especially at night, eased by shaking the hand.
carpien.whatHappens: The median nerve runs with the finger tendons under a fibrous band at the front of the wrist. When it is compressed there, the thumb, index, middle finger and half of the ring finger go numb.
carpien.whoIsAffected: More often women, between 40 and 60, pregnancy, repeated wrist movements.
carpien.warning: Loss of thumb strength, dropping things, constant numbness: see a doctor.

arthmain.name: Hand osteoarthritis
arthmain.whatYouFeel: Pain and stiffness in the end joints of the fingers, knobbly joints, difficulty gripping and unscrewing.
arthmain.whatHappens: The cartilage of the small finger joints wears. Painful flare-ups alternate with calm periods, then the nodules become painless.
arthmain.whoIsAffected: Over 50, more often women, often several people in the same family.
arthmain.warning: Red, hot and very swollen joint, or fever: see a doctor the same day. Several swollen joints at the base of the fingers or in the wrists, on both sides, with morning stiffness lasting more than 30 minutes: see a doctor promptly, inflammatory arthritis is best treated early.

rhiz.name: Thumb base osteoarthritis
rhiz.commonName: Arthritis at the base of the thumb
rhiz.whatYouFeel: Pain at the base of the thumb when pinching, turning a key, opening a jar.
rhiz.whatHappens: The cartilage wears between the trapezium and the first metacarpal, the joint that lets the thumb oppose the fingers.
rhiz.warning: Thumb that changes shape or constant pain: see a doctor.

ressaut.name: Trigger finger
ressaut.whatYouFeel: Finger that locks bent then releases with a click, pain at the base of the finger on the palm side, especially in the morning.
ressaut.whatHappens: The flexor tendon slides under a pulley at the base of the finger. A thickening of the tendon or the pulley makes it catch.
ressaut.warning: Locked finger that no longer straightens: see a doctor. Emergency the same day: a finger that is red, swollen along its whole length and very painful when straightened, especially after a prick, a splinter or a cut, or with fever. An infection of the tendon sheath needs urgent surgery.

quervain.name: De Quervain's tenosynovitis
quervain.commonName: Wrist pain on the thumb side
quervain.whatYouFeel: Pain at the edge of the wrist on the thumb side when grasping, wringing or lifting a child.
quervain.whatHappens: Two thumb tendons slide in a sheath at the edge of the wrist. The sheath thickens and the passage becomes painful.
quervain.whoIsAffected: New parents carrying a baby, repeated thumb movements.
quervain.warning: No improvement after 6 weeks: see a doctor, an injection is often effective.

kyste.name: Wrist ganglion cyst
kyste.commonName: Lump on the back of the wrist
kyste.whatYouFeel: Firm lump on the back of the wrist that changes size, sometimes uncomfortable when leaning on the hand.
kyste.whatHappens: A pocket of joint fluid forms from the joint, most often near the scapholunate ligament. It is harmless and goes away on its own in half of cases.
kyste.warning: Lump that grows quickly, is painful, or makes the fingers numb: see a doctor.

dupuytren.name: Dupuytren's disease
dupuytren.whatYouFeel: A nodule then a hard cord in the palm, ring and little fingers that no longer straighten fully, without pain.
dupuytren.whatHappens: The tissue under the skin of the palm thickens and contracts, forming cords that pull the fingers.
dupuytren.whoIsAffected: Men over 50, Northern European origin, family history.
dupuytren.warning: Exercises do not stop the disease from progressing. When the hand no longer lies flat on a table, see a doctor: a procedure is possible.

entorse.name: Wrist sprain
entorse.whatYouFeel: Pain on the back of the wrist when leaning on it, swelling, loss of grip strength.
entorse.whatHappens: Falling on the hand stretches the wrist ligaments. A fracture of the scaphoid or the radius, or a tear of the ligament between the scaphoid and the lunate, can give the same signs as a simple sprain.
entorse.whoIsAffected: Fall on an outstretched hand, board and contact sports.
entorse.warning: After a fall on the hand, see a doctor within 24 to 48 hours for an X-ray if: pain in the hollow at the base of the thumb, deformed wrist, a lot of swelling, unable to grip or turn the hand. Start exercises only once a fracture has been ruled out. Pain lasting more than two weeks despite a normal X-ray: go back to the doctor.

tfcc.name: Triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC) injury
tfcc.commonName: Wrist pain on the little-finger side when leaning
tfcc.whatYouFeel: Pain at the edge of the wrist on the little-finger side when leaning on the hand or turning a key, sometimes a click.
tfcc.whatHappens: This complex of fibrocartilage and ligaments, between the head of the ulna and the carpal bones, cushions weight-bearing and stabilises the joint between the radius and the ulna at the wrist.
tfcc.whoIsAffected: After a fall on the hand, gymnasts, racket sports.
tfcc.warning: Unstable wrist or pain lasting more than 6 weeks: see a doctor.

ecu.name: Extensor carpi ulnaris tendinopathy
ecu.commonName: Pain at the edge of the wrist on the little-finger side
ecu.whatYouFeel: Pain on the back of the wrist on the little-finger side, when turning the forearm or tilting the hand.
ecu.whatHappens: This tendon runs in a groove over the head of the ulna, where it becomes irritated or unstable.
ecu.whoIsAffected: Tennis, golf, rowers, twisting movements of the wrist.
ecu.warning: Painful snapping of the tendon when rotating: see a doctor.

scaphoide.name: Scaphoid fracture
scaphoide.commonName: Pain at the base of the thumb after a fall
scaphoide.whatYouFeel: Pain in the hollow at the base of the thumb, on the back of the wrist, when leaning and gripping, often with little swelling.
scaphoide.whatHappens: The scaphoid has a poor blood supply and heals slowly. The fracture does not always show on the first X-ray.
scaphoide.whoIsAffected: Young adults after a fall on an outstretched hand.
scaphoide.warning: After a fall, pain in the hollow at the base of the thumb means seeing a doctor within 24 to 48 hours, even if the X-ray is normal: a splint is applied while waiting for an MRI or a repeat X-ray. A neglected fracture may not heal.

guyon.name: Ulnar nerve compression at the wrist
guyon.whatYouFeel: Pins and needles in the little and ring fingers, weakness when spreading the fingers, no pain at the elbow.
guyon.whatHappens: The ulnar nerve runs through a channel between the pisiform and the hamate, where prolonged pressure from the heel of the hand compresses it.
guyon.whoIsAffected: Cyclists, people using vibrating tools or crutches.
guyon.warning: Wasting of the hand muscles or clumsiness: see a doctor.

ouvfer.name: Open and close the hand
ouvfer.how: Gentle fist then fingers spread. 10 times, ideally in warm water.

opp.name: Thumb opposition
opp.how: Touch the tip of each finger with the thumb. 5 rounds.

balle.name: Squeeze a soft ball
balle.how: Squeeze for 3 s without pain. 10 times.

attn.name: Night splint
attn.how: Wrist held straight during sleep, for 6 weeks.
attn.videoSearch: carpal tunnel night splint how to wear

gliss.name: Tendon glides
gliss.how: Move through open hand, hook, fist, tabletop. 10 cycles, 3 times a day.

nmed.name: Median nerve glide
nmed.how: Arm by your side, elbow bent. Extend the wrist and fingers backwards while tilting the head to the same side, then relax. 5 repetitions, 3 times a day, with no pins and needles.
nmed.videoSearch: median nerve glide carpal tunnel exercise

attp.name: Thumb splint
attp.how: Wear it for painful tasks and at night for 3 to 6 weeks.
attp.videoSearch: thumb splint thumb arthritis De Quervain

ecart.name: Spread the thumb against a band
ecart.how: Band around the fingers, move the thumb away. 3 sets of 10.
ecart.videoSearch: thumb abductor strengthening band thumb arthritis

isop.name: Spread the thumb against resistance
isop.how: Push the thumb against the other hand without moving. Hold 30 s, 5 times.

excp.name: Slow lowering with a light weight
excp.how: Wrist on the edge of a table, thumb up, lower over 4 s. 3 sets of 10.
excp.videoSearch: De Quervain eccentric radial deviation exercise

repos.name: Relative rest from gripping
repos.how: Limit tight, repeated grips, use thicker tool handles.
repos.videoSearch: joint protection hand tips occupational therapy

etdoigt.name: Finger extension stretch
etdoigt.how: Lay the hand flat on a table and press gently. 5 times 15 s.
etdoigt.videoSearch: finger extension stretch Dupuytren trigger finger

poign.name: Wrist bending and straightening
poign.how: Forearm resting, raise and lower the hand. 2 sets of 15.

isopoign.name: Wrist extension hold
isopoign.how: Wrist straight, resist the other hand pressing down. Hold 20 s, 5 times.

prosup.name: Forearm rotation
prosup.how: Elbow at your side, turn the palm up then down. 2 sets of 15.

devuln.name: Wrist tilt against resistance
devuln.how: Little-finger edge towards the floor against a band, return slowly. 3 sets of 10.

nuln.name: Ulnar nerve glide
nuln.how: Arm out to the side, palm towards the ceiling. Bend the elbow bringing the hand towards the ear while tilting the head the other way, then come back. 5 slow repetitions, with no lasting pins and needles.

appui.name: Take pressure off the heel of the hand
appui.how: Bike handlebars, tools, crutches: change your grip or add padding.
appui.videoSearch: ulnar nerve compression wrist cyclist tips

immob.name: Immobilisation and allowed movements
immob.how: Keep the prescribed splint or cast on, without removing it. Move the shoulder, elbow and the fingers that stick out freely, several times a day. Do not grip objects or lean on the hand until the doctor agrees.
